text: On David Lewis's 1976 analysis, what constitutes time travel?
choices: A discrepancy between the traveler's personal time and external time: the duration of the journey measured by external time does not equal its duration measured by the traveler's own personal time.
Any physical transportation of an object from an earlier moment of external time to a later one.
The presence of a closed timelike curve in the background spacetime along which the traveler moves.
A reversal of the thermodynamic arrow of time in the region immediately surrounding the traveler.
explanation: Lewis defines time travel as a systematic divergence between personal time (the traveler's own clocks and biological processes) and external time (the time coordinate of the background spacetime). Mere transportation forward is what a rock sitting in the ground undergoes, with no such discrepancy, so it is not time travel (choice 1). The definition is explicitly neutral about mechanism, so a closed timelike curve is one possible means but not part of the analysis (choice 2), and no reversal of thermodynamic processes is required (choice 3).
